reason.heat: {month}: {crop} at the {stage} stage, while this area averages {value} days above {threshold} °C.
reason.drought: In {value}% of past years, {month} had a dry spell of 10+ days ({crop}, {stage} stage).
reason.water_deficit: {month}: rain falls about {value} mm short of what the crops lose to evaporation ({crop}, {stage} stage).
reason.frost: {month}: about {value} frost days on average ({crop}, {stage} stage).
reason.waterlogging: {month}: about {value} heavy-rain days on average, and this soil drains slowly ({crop}, {stage} stage).
reason.soil_drying: {month}: soil moisture has been below normal in recent years, {value} standard deviations ({crop}, {stage} stage).

action.heat: Consider earlier sowing or a more heat-tolerant variety so the {stage} stage avoids {month}. Ask your extension office.
action.drought: Keep crop residue or mulch on the soil to hold moisture, and plan a backup irrigation if you can.
action.water_deficit: Plan about {value} mm of irrigation for {month}, or consider a crop that needs less water.
action.frost: Shift the sowing date so the {stage} stage misses {month}, or choose a frost-tolerant variety.
action.waterlogging: Use raised beds or drainage channels, and avoid sowing just before the heavy-rain season.
action.soil_drying: Keep residue on the field and check soil moisture before deciding to irrigate.

why.current: This is what is farmed here today. It is the baseline the other options are compared with.
why.current_alt_rice_wheat: This is a common rotation in central Punjab. It is the baseline the other options are compared with.
why.water_saver: Suggested to lower the farm's water demand: it uses crops that need less water or handle drought better.
why.soil_builder: Suggested to rebuild the soil: it adds nitrogen-fixing legumes, more ground cover and more crop families.
why.water_change_less: It needs about {pct}% less water per year than your current rotation ({new} mm instead of {old} mm).
why.water_change_more: It needs about {pct}% more water per year than your current rotation ({new} mm instead of {old} mm).
why.cover_change: The field is bare about {months} fewer months per year.

evidence.heat: {month}: {crop} at the {stage} stage, while this area averages {days} days above {threshold} °C.
evidence.deficit: {month} is a water-critical month for {crop}, but rain ({precip} mm) is far below evaporation demand ({et0} mm): a gap of {deficit} mm to cover by irrigation or stored soil water.
evidence.dry_spell: In {pct}% of the last {years} years, {month} had a dry spell of 10+ days during the {stage} stage of {crop}.
evidence.frost: {month}: {crop} at the {stage} stage, with about {days} frost days in this area.
evidence.erosion_bare: The field is bare in {months}, when heavy-rain days still happen (about {days} per year). Bare soil in heavy rain washes away.
evidence.drought_years: Recent drought years in the 20-year record: {years}.
evidence.sm_dry: Soil moisture in {month} has been below normal in recent years ({z} standard deviations).
evidence.low_om: Soil organic matter is low (about {om}%). Legumes, cover crops and crop residue help raise it.
evidence.high_erodibility: The soil is {texture} with a lot of silt, which washes away easily when bare.

benefits.familiar: Familiar crops, equipment and markets: no new skills or buyers needed.
benefits.n_fixing: Nitrogen-fixing crops ({crops}) take nitrogen from the air, so the next crop needs less fertilizer.
benefits.cover: Cover crops ({crops}) protect the soil between main crops from heavy rain and wind.
benefits.deep_roots: Deep-rooted crops ({crops}) open the soil so rain soaks in instead of running off.
benefits.families: {n} different crop families break pest and disease cycles (your current rotation has {current}).
benefits.drought_tolerant: Drought-tolerant crops ({crops}) handle dry spells better than the crops they replace.
benefits.forage: Fodder crops ({crops}) can feed animals or bring extra income.

info_gaps.tier_standard: Based on NASA POWER climate data for a ~50 km area. No satellite soil-moisture or vegetation data was loaded for this exact point.
info_gaps.tier_featured: Satellite soil moisture (SMAP, 9 km) and vegetation (MODIS NDVI, 250 m) describe the area, not your individual field.
info_gaps.tier_us_enhanced: Ground data (PRISM weather, SSURGO soil, CDL crop history) is used, but there is no soil test from this field.
info_gaps.smap_short: Satellite soil moisture only exists since 2015 ({years} years), so 'normal' is based on a short record.
info_gaps.income: Income values are rough regional placeholders, not local prices.
info_gaps.calendar_approx: Sowing and harvest months are typical regional values and may differ on your farm.
info_gaps.no_soil: Soil data is not available for this point, so soil effects are estimated with less certainty.
info_gaps.ndvi_mismatch: Satellites saw low vegetation in {observed}, but this rotation expects bare soil in {expected}. Your real calendar may differ from the template.
info_gaps.scenario: These results use a What-If scenario ({temp} °C, {rain}% rain), not observed weather.

local_review.soil_test: Get a soil test (nutrients, organic matter, salinity) before changing the rotation.
local_review.planting_dates: Confirm sowing and harvest dates with your local agriculture extension office.
local_review.market: Check that there are buyers or a use for {crops} near you.
local_review.equipment: {crops} may need extra equipment or labour (for example haying, puddling or transplanting).
local_review.rice_water: Rice needs a lot of water: confirm canal or tubewell supply for the whole season.
local_review.pest_history: Ask about local pest and disease history for the new crops ({crops}).
local_review.drainage: This soil drains slowly: check for waterlogging before sowing {crops}.
local_review.irrigation: Rain covers only part of the crop water need here: confirm how much irrigation water you can count on.
